subject: Acme AI streaming SLO alignment & reproducibility probe
messages:
From: Samantha Owens <samantha@acme.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme AI streaming SLOs & initial benchmark info

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + couple open asks so we can align the trial: 

- Target production SLOs: 95th p50 latency target of 220ms for streaming token-first-byte, sustained concurrency 120 requests/sec for our B2B chat flows, and burst to 350 for short windows.
- Typical request shape: short prompts (12–40 tokens) followed by streaming generation (avg 180 tokens).
- Data: we cannot share PII but can provide sanitized prompt/turn examples (attached).

Open asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood reproduce token-level streaming latency (TTFB and per-token latency) in a repeatable run?
2) What measurement definitions you will use (start-of-stream, token-delays, backpressure) and how you will capture KV cache warm/cold behavior?
3) A proposed 2-hour run window (off-hours) where we can validate against our traffic shape — is that feasible?

I attached a small sample prompt file (sanitized). Happy to set up a short run checklist next week.

Thanks,
Samantha Owens
Head of Infrastructure, Acme AI
Samantha@acme.ai

Attachment: acme_prompt_samples_v1.jsonl (3KB, JSONL; sanitized examples)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Owens <samantha@acme.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI streaming SLOs & initial benchmark info

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear recap and the prompt samples. Quick confirmation and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Measurement definitions (we will send a short spec PDF):
   - stream_start_ttfb: wall-clock delta between request reception at ingress and first-byte emitted by runtime.
   - inter_token_latency: median and 95th of per-token emission gaps during streaming.
   - end_to_end_latency: time from request start to final token emitted.
   - cold_vs_warm: explicit warmup runs + tracked KV cache hits; we will tag each request as warm/cold in logs.

2) Repro strategy: deterministic prompt set (your attached file) + seeded model run where applicable, repeated 3x across different infra nodes; aggregate median/95th. We'll provide raw per-token traces and a summarized CSV.

3) Run window: 2-hour off-hours window is fine. Can we propose Tue Aug 11 01:00–03:00 UTC? That aligns with our maintenance window and gives our SRE time to instrument.

Action items:
- Ben: I asked Ben to draft the reproducibility checklist and the minimal tracing payload we need.
- Monica: will coordinate log access and any ACLs for your account.
- Samantha: if Aug 11 works, confirm and we'll schedule infra.

I'll attach an initial spec (redwood_streaming_spec_v0.3.pdf) and a run-window checklist in spreadsheet form.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_streaming_spec_v0.3.pdf, run-window-checklist.xlsx

From: Samantha Owens <samantha@acme.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI streaming SLOs & initial benchmark info

Thanks Vivek — Aug 11 01:00–03:00 UTC works on our side. A couple clarifying points before the run: 

- Model seeding: we'll be using an open LLM (gpt-lite-3) and can provide a fixed checkpoint; please confirm Redwood can pin the version for the run.
- Tokenization differences: we see slight tokenization variance across runtimes. Will you normalize token counts or report both token counts + byte offsets?
- Observability: we need per-request IDs included in the CSV so we can cross-reference with our telemetry.

Ravi will be the technical lead on our side during the slot (cc'd). We'll also compile a small failure-mode list to watch (time-limited responses, partial streams).

Samantha

To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme AI streaming SLOs — instrumentation notes

Forwarding the thread to SRE for run-day instrumentation notes. Laura — surface-read below then see my quick checklist at the bottom.

-- quoted --
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI streaming SLOs & initial benchmark info

(see earlier)

-- end quoted --

Laura — baseline checklist I propose for the run: 
- Ensure request IDs are propagated from ingress through runtime and into per-token trace files.
- Snapshot kernel/cuda metrics every 30s (util, mem, kernel-wait).
- Capture queue depth and batch sizes per inference cycle.
- Mark warmup phase (first 5 minutes) and exclude from SLA calculations, but keep traces.
- Provide a short script to replay the prompt set against a pinned model and capture start-of-stream timestamps.

I attached a draft script and the run-window checklist. If we need a longer warmup for KV cache, say +10m, flag it.

Ben
Principal Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: run-window-checklist.xlsx

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI streaming SLOs — instrumentation notes

All — quick confirmation from SRE side. We can support the proposed telemetry and will do the following during the Tue Aug 11 run (post-run notes to follow):

- We'll pin model checkpoint as requested and run three iterations separated by 15 minutes to reduce node-local cache coupling.
- Tokenization: we'll emit both token-count and byte-offset columns in the trace so you can reconcile differences.
- We'll include request_id and hubspot run_id in every CSV row (format: acme-ACME-2026-43-r1).
- Warmup: we recommend 10-minute warmup per node cluster; will exclude warmup from SLA calc but retain data.
- We'll also capture backpressure events and HTTP chunk timings to help debug partial streams.

Next: Vivek, could you confirm whether we should forward raw traces to Acme or upload to a shared Drive link first?

Laura Bennett
SRE Manager — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Owens <samantha@acme.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ravi Shah <ravi@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI streaming SLOs & initial benchmark info

Samantha / Ravi —

Solid — thanks everyone. Confirming final run plan: 

- Run window: Tue Aug 11 01:00–03:00 UTC (10-minute warmup per node, three full iterations).
- Deliverables: per-token CSVs, summarized median/95th tables, raw traces, and a short run playbook with observed anomalies. We'll upload everything to the Drive link in related_links and share access to your team.
- Next steps for Acme: please provide the pinned checkpoint reference and authorize Drive access for laura_bennett@redwood.ai.

I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute pre-run sync 2026-08-11 23:00 UTC to walk through the checklist.

Thanks,
Vivek
